listen: Good morning. This is The Daily Brief for Monday, November 16. Our lead story is from Anthropic. The company has filed a registration statement on Form S-1 with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. The filing relates to its proposed initial public offering of Class A common stock. An S-1 is the document a company files when it plans to offer shares to the public. Anthropic has also launched a roadshow for the proposed offering. And it says it is committing a portion of its shares to the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, a new entity whose stake increases as the company grows. The announcements give no details on pricing, size or timing. Now to the front page. In football, the San Francisco 49ers beat the Dallas Cowboys 46 to 40. They racked up 584 yards, led by Brock Purdy, Christian McCaffrey and Deebo Samuel. In basketball, the Houston Rockets beat the Washington Wizards 147 to 119 for their fourth straight win. Amen Thompson scored 26 points and Kevin Durant added 25. Now the sections. In tech, Simon Willison released a new Datasette plugin that combines MapLibre with OpenFreeMap, built mostly from a single prompt. In politics, The Lever reports that twenty-one Senate Democrats advanced a lame-duck permitting bill that could speed fossil fuel infrastructure for data centers. NPR reports Montana is sending a Democrat to the U.S. House for the first time in three decades. In world news, the UK, Australia, Canada and Italy say Israeli authorities are holding back vital supplies at the borders, and they are calling for rapid humanitarian access to Gaza. Separately, Saudi-backed Yemeni forces say they are moving troops from the Bab al-Mandab Strait to defend Aden, leaving the Houthis in control of the coastal area. In sports, both champions kept their titles at UFC 334, and the Braves agreed to a three-year, 35 million dollar deal with reliever Evan Phillips. In Atlanta, Dunwoody is asking for public input on a draft unified development ordinance, and two more Westside developments are set for groundbreakings. In architecture, a new add-on brings BIM elements, drawings, schedules and IFC to SketchUp for smaller practices. Ricoh has also launched a rugged 360 degree camera for construction. In science, today's Astronomy Picture of the Day shows star formation with jets in NGC 7129, as seen by Webb. And NASA says the ice near the summit of Indonesia's Puncak Jaya has shrunk to scattered patches. That is the brief. Have a good day.

lead.title: Anthropic files S-1 with the SEC for proposed initial public offering Today, Anthropic, PBC filed a registration statement on Form S-1 with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission relating to its proposed initial public offering of its Class A common stock.
lead.note: Anthropic, PBC has filed a registration statement on Form S-1 with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. It relates to the company's proposed initial public offering of Class A common stock. An S-1 is the filing a company makes with the SEC when it plans to offer shares to the public. Two related Anthropic announcements accompany it: a roadshow for the proposed offering, and a commitment of a portion of its shares to the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, a new entity whose stake increases as the company grows. For a reader who builds tools with Claude, it shows how the company behind the model is organizing its finances. The announcements as listed give no details on pricing, size or timing of the offering.
